subject: people who peaked in high school
tagline: SpaceX for people who peaked in high school
one_liner: Aerospace-grade telemetry for the highest point of your life, which has already happened.
brand_voice_notes: An launch-services company that has quietly become an awards program. It speaks in flight-test language about a person's life: the peak is an apogee, achievements are burns, a class reunion is an atmospheric reentry event. Never consoling, never mocking. It reports the trajectory the way a range officer reports a range officer's numbers, and it considers the descent a normal and fully expected part of the mission profile.

hero.h1: You peaked. We have the flight data.
hero.sub: Apogee reconstructs the exact week your trajectory turned over, issues a certificate, then holds you at a stable and survivable altitude for the remaining forty years.

features.title: Apogee reconstruction
features.blurb: Submit one yearbook, three group photographs and a regional newspaper clipping. Our range team triangulates the week the trajectory turned over, accurate to within nine days, and issues a numbered certificate.

features.title: Sustainer burns
features.blurb: Correctly sized achievements, fired quarterly, to hold altitude. A promotion to Senior. A half marathon at a respectable pace. Enough thrust to maintain. Never enough to climb.

features.title: Reentry shielding
features.blurb: Reunion invitations, tagged photographs and messages beginning with the word remember are intercepted at the boundary layer and answered on your behalf in a professional tone.

pricing_tiers.name: Suborbital
pricing_tiers.tagline: You go up. You come down. You are home in time for dinner.
perks: Apogee date verified to the week

pricing_tiers.name: Legacy program

demo_screen_concept: A range-control 'Trajectory Console' for a single customer, Dale Renfro. A left dossier rail carries his portrait, class year, current altitude and a descent-rate readout. The centre plots his life as an SVG flight path: a brass parabola with a marked apogee tick and a long dashed descending tail, with burn markers along it that reveal a life event on hover. The right rail is the burn log, every thrust event listed with tabular figures and an arm/safe toggle on the next scheduled sustainer burn. Tabs switch between TRAJECTORY, BURN LOG and REENTRY. A 'schedule next launch window' control returns a date that is always already in the past.

images.rationale: Hero skipped because the direction is banner-typographic (Anton caps against a brass shelf rule) and a photograph would have fought the type. Demo got one asset: the console's dossier rail shows the customer's archived peak, which is literally a photograph, so a faded 1990s trophy-night print earns its place. The remaining budget went to the three named testimonials as deadpan corporate headshots of people who were athletic twenty-five years ago, shot against the page's own navy so they sit in the felt rather than on it.

design_direction.style: Varsity trophy-case awards program, night-of-the-banquet dark mode. The page is staged as the printed awards programme and engraved trophy wall of a heavily funded launch-services company that has decided a person's best year is a flight regime and files the class of 2009 under mission archive. A deep varsity navy ground (#12182B) runs the whole page with no light mode, no glass, no backdrop blur, no aurora washes, no clay volume, no bento lattice, no paper stock, no print hairline frames and no drawing-sheet chrome: every surface is a flat felt panel one step lighter (#1A2138) inside a 1px brass hairline at a uniform 2px radius, corners kept near-square because this company engraves things. Depth comes only from the trophy motif: a 2px brass rule running along the top edge of every panel like the engraved plate screwed to the base of an award, never a shadow, never a glow. The organising move is the case: content is laid out as rows of shelved panels of equal height butted at a 16px gutter above a continuous brass shelf rule, so every section reads as a row of trophies rather than a row of cards. The core motif is the chenille patch: a felt shield with a stitched zigzag border built in pure CSS (a repeating-linear-gradient notched edge over a flat fill), carrying a single numeral or letter in cream, used as the list bullet, the feature index, the pricing tier badge, the testimonial portrait frame and the section marker, so every discrete item on the page reads as something that was awarded. The second motif is the apogee arc: an SVG parabola in a 1px brass stroke that rises to a marked tick and then falls away as a dashed tail, hemming every section break and drawn once on reveal, so the reader is never more than one screen away from the shape of the descent. One trophy brass (#C8A548) is the sole carrier: the wordmark, every primary CTA, one word per headline, every shelf rule and every patch border, always as a flat flood or a hairline with navy knocked out of it. One rationed descent red (#C4462F) is quarantined strictly to decline telemetry (altitude lost since the peak, years elapsed, negative descent rates, denied altitude requests, the fuel-remaining line in pricing) and appears nowhere decorative, so the only warm colour on a cold page is always the number going down. Anton sets the wordmark and headlines in heavy banner caps at monumental sizes with athletic-department confidence, tracking tightened to -0.02em at display sizes and set flush left against the shelf rule. Spectral carries plain, faintly awards-programme body copy at 17px with a 1.62 line-height, italicised only inside testimonial quotes. Every figure that pretends to be flight telemetry (apogee dates, altitudes in metres, descent rates, burn durations, fuel remaining, tier prices) is set in IBM Plex Mono with tabular figures inside recessed navy wells one step darker than the felt, so it reads like the range log, not marketing. No light mode, no glass, no blur, no gradients on type, no neon, no clay shadow pairs, no offset sticker shadows, no bento lattice, no hairline print frames, no hatch fills, no didone engraving, no split-flap numerals, no supergraphic arcs, no roundels, no HUD corner brackets, no drawing-sheet title blocks, no engraved seals, no photographic press plates, no mirrored type, no emoji. Reads like a company that files your best year under 'archive' and considers the descent a normal part of the mission profile.
design_direction.archetype: Trophy-wall product landing page: hero claim over a shelf rule, three shelved feature panels, a testimonial row of chenille-framed portraits, a three-tier awards pricing case, and a single console CTA.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Banquet-restrained. The apogee arc draws once on reveal over 900ms and its dashed tail fades in behind it. Shelf rules wipe left to right on section reveal. Chenille patches rotate two degrees and settle on hover with no lift and no scale. CTAs invert to a brass flood on hover and depress 1px on press. The descent-rate digit steps once per second in red. Sections fade up 6px with a 40ms stagger. All gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Full-width navy field. Brass eyebrow mono label reading the mission designation, then the h1 in Anton banner caps at clamp(3rem, 9vw, 7.5rem) set flush left against a 2px brass shelf rule that runs the full measure beneath it. The subhead sits in a narrow 58-character Spectral column at the left. To its right, an SVG apogee arc rises to a brass tick labelled with a mono apogee date and falls away as a dashed red-tinted tail into the fold. Beneath, a brass-flood primary CTA and a recessed telemetry well carrying three figures: apogee date, altitude lost, and years since. No hero photograph.
